name: The Dark Iron War
summary: At Dun Modr, on the Wetlands' northern edge, Motley Garmason leads a desperate defense. The Dark Iron clan holds the town after saboteurs shattered the Thandol Span, leaving the Ironforge Mountaineers with a tenuous line as they wait for reinforcements that may never come.

sections.title: A Front at the Northern Gate
sections.body: Dun Modr guarded the southern end of the colossal Thandol Span, the bridge linking Khaz Modan to Lordaeron. Dark Iron saboteurs and demolitionists shattered its archway, severing Alliance travel before they overran the stronghold. Motley Garmason and a handful of surviving defenders withdrew to an observation camp just outside town. Without a counterattack, the northern gateway risks permanent Dark Iron dominion.

sections.title: Buying Time for the Reserves
sections.body: Dwarven regiments are deployed to distant Alliance battlefields, leaving Motley's small detachment largely to fend for itself. His scouts try to signal Ironforge for relief, but communications falter and promised reserves remain out of sight. To buy time and disrupt the enemy's entrenchments, Motley orders surgical strikes into Dun Modr's ruins. The aim is to thin the ranks of Dark Iron engineers, tunnelers, and front-line soldiers before they push farther south into the Wetlands.

faq.answer: Motley Garmason is an Ironforge Mountaineer officer commanding Dun Modr's surviving garrison. From a camp just outside the occupied town, he coordinates scouting and guerrilla strikes against the Dark Iron forces.

faq.q: Why is Dun Modr so important to Ironforge?
faq.answer: Dun Modr guards the southern foot of the Thandol Span. The span is the sole overland highway linking Khaz Modan to the Arathi Highlands and northern Lordaeron, so control of Dun Modr means control of ground travel and supplies between those regions.

faq.q: Why are Dark Iron dwarves fighting in the Wetlands?
faq.answer: The Dark Iron clan has long sought to undermine their Bronzebeard cousins and weaken the Alliance. By invading the Wetlands and destroying the Thandol Span, they cut Ironforge's supply lines to the north and open a hostile second front behind Alliance borders.

faq.q: What happened to the Thandol Span?
faq.answer: Dark Iron tunnelers and demolitionists planted concentrated explosives in the Thandol Span's foundational arches, severely damaging the bridge. They meant to cut off Ironforge reinforcements from Lordaeron before overrunning Dun Modr.

faq.q: Where are the Ironforge reserve forces?
faq.answer: Ironforge's military is stretched across campaigns abroad and defenses at home. Garmason's scout, Roggo, struggles to reach high command reliably, leaving the Dun Modr outpost to hold the line with whatever local allies it can find.

faq.q: What happens after pushing back the Dark Irons in Dun Modr?
aliases: next quest after dark iron war
what follows the dark iron war
faq.answer: Clearing the foot soldiers and sappers buys crucial time. Roggo's intelligence reveals that Kam Deepfury, held in the Stormwind Stockade, helped plan the attack on the Thandol Span, and Motley asks you to bring him Deepfury's head.

angles.text: As a Bronzebeard dwarf, you know Dun Modr's loss is a bitter humiliation and a direct threat to Khaz Modan's sovereignty. Vengeance against ancestral enemies is called for.
As an Alliance member, you know the Thandol Span's destruction and Dun Modr's fall sever overland access between Stormwind's northern allies and the southern kingdoms.
As an engineer, you can see the Dark Iron saboteurs' specialized explosives reveal a chilling mastery of structural demolition.
